R1043:
Since early 2026, the conflict in Sudan has evolved from a humanitarian crisis affecting Chad into a direct security threat to eastern border areas. Repeated drone strikes, cross-border incursions, and clashes involving fighters aligned with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have already caused casualties on Chadian territory, including around Tine and other border regions. These incidents indicate a growing risk that the Sudan conflict could generate sustained military confrontations, proxy violence, or retaliatory attacks inside Chad. This risk is increasingly characterised by the possibility of sustained military confrontation on Chadian territory involving RSF, SAF-aligned groups, and associated proxy forces operating along the Chad–Sudan border.
This risk is driven by a convergence of security, economic, and political factors. The Chad–Sudan border has become a strategic corridor for the movement of fuel, arms, gold, and military supplies supporting groups involved in the Sudan conflict. Competition over these routes has transformed border areas into contested spaces where violence increasingly follows smuggling and supply networks. Recent attacks suggest a shift from incidental spillover to deliberate projection of force into Chadian territory.
The conflict is also aggravating existing vulnerabilities in Chad. Fractures within cross-border Zaghawa community networks, which remain influential within Chad’s security apparatus, have deepened as communities react to violence in Darfur and perceptions of Chad’s involvement in the conflict. Continued violence in Darfur, combined with Chad’s historical role in Sudanese proxy conflicts, increases the risk of elite defections, armed realignments, and renewed cross-border mobilisation. Historical patterns of proxy warfare between Chad and Sudan may also re-emerge, including support to armed groups and militias operating across the border, increasing the likelihood of retaliatory attacks and further regional destabilisation.
Over the next one to three months, further RSF incursions, SAF-backed proxy activity, or competition over border corridors could increase cross-border violence, displacement, protection risks, and humanitarian needs in eastern Chad. Additional attacks or retaliations would likely worsen conditions in provinces already hosting large numbers of refugees and returnees, further straining regional services, humanitarian operations, and community relations. The risk is not limited to humanitarian spillover and increasingly involves the possibility of sustained confrontation on Chadian territory involving RSF, SAF-aligned groups, and associated proxy forces. ([Africa Center for Strategic Studies 09/03/2026](https://africacenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Chad-Risks-Instability.pdf), [ACLED 08/04/2026](https://acleddata.com/update/africa-overview-april-2026), [Global Initiative 06/03/2026](https://globalinitiative.net/analysis/how-border-criminal-economies-are-drawing-chad-further-into-sudans-conflict/), [ISS Africa 03/04/2025](https://issafrica.org/iss-today/urgent-au-action-could-defuse-rising-chad-sudan-tensions), [RFI 13/05/2026](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20260513-tchad-de-nouvelles-frappes-enregistr%C3%A9es-%C3%A0-la-fronti%C3%A8re-soudanaise-font-craindre-le-pire), [UNHCR 18/05/2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/chad/core-emergency-situation-chad-update-arrivals-sudan-17-may-2026), [UNFPA 15/05/2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/chad/unfpa-situation-report-chad-humanitarian-response-1-30-april-2026))
R1048:
The RSF offensive launched in early 2026 against Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) positions in Baw county opened a new front in Blue Nile state. This has significantly increased the likelihood of conflict spreading to previously unaffected areas to the north, particularly Ed Damazine, the state capital, as well as the strategic corridor leading to the Roseires Dam. By advancing in Blue Nile state, RSF seeks to strengthen its position to recapture and control central Sudan, later opening a route through Sennar state.
Following heavy territorial losses in 2025, including entire states in central Sudan, RSF has reconstituted its operational capacity through its alliance with Abdelaziz Adam al Hilu's Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N/Al Hilu). Access to terrain under its control has provided RSF with defensive depth, cross-border supply lines, and logistical continuity. This enables it to sustain multifront operations and power its advance in Blue Nile, positioning the RSF for a prolonged and expanded offensive rather than a short-term tactical push and increasing the likelihood of escalation beyond the current front lines.
External facilitation further compounds these dynamics. SAF has repeatedly accused South Sudan and Ethiopia of enabling this mobilisation, with satellite imagery from February 2026 showing a logistics camp near the Ethiopian border in Benishangul Gumz despite official Ethiopian denial. If sustained, such external support would significantly raise the possibility of a scaled-up offensive by insulating RSF operations from battlefield setbacks ([ACLED 26/01/2026](https://acleddata.com/report/blue-nile-peripheral-front-central-battleground-sudan-conflict ), [MEE 26/01/2026](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/sudans-rsf-launches-offensive-blue-nile-state), [AJ 19/08/2025](https://www.aljazeera.com/features/longform/2025/8/19/inside-the-nuba-mountains-and-the-alliance-reshaping-sudans-civil-war ), [ACLED 15/04/2025](https://acleddata.com/report/two-years-war-sudan-how-saf-gaining-upper-hand), [ICG 07/04/2025](https://www.crisisgroup.org/stm/africa/sudan/two-years-sudans-war-spreading), [Reuters 10/02/2026](https://www.reuters.com/investigations/ethiopia-builds-secret-camp-train-sudan-rsf-fighters-sources-say-2026-02-10/ ), [ST 25/01/2026](https://sudantribune.com/article/309824))
R0993:
On 25 March 2025, the new US administration – under President Donald Trump – reached an agreement with Ukraine and Russia on a temporary 30-day pause in attacks on energy infrastructure. Ukraine agreed with the US on a list of energy facilities that Russia should stop attacking, although Russia took some oil and gas production facilities off the list and has continued attacking them.
It is unclear whether this partial ceasefire applies to the use of long-range missiles and drones or artillery. The full details of the partial ceasefire have not been made public. Energy infrastructure located near the front line remains vulnerable to damage.
Given the history of Russian forces violating ceasefire agreements since 2014, they are likely to also violate this agreement and resort to disinformation and false flag attacks to conceal the violations, possibly blaming Ukraine for disrupting the ceasefire agreement. In this context, US officials may downplay these violations to claim the success of the US-led ceasefire.
Russian forces, having stockpiled missiles and drones for use against the energy sector, may step up their attacks on civilian infrastructure, such as residential areas, as a sustained political tactic especially following the US-led negotiations for a full ceasefire. A recent such attack was on 4 April, which targeted a residential area in Kryvyi Rih city, Dnipropetrovska, killing 19 people (including 9 children). Alternatively, Russian forces could accumulate the missiles and drones that they planned to use in 2024 then launch a major countrywide combined missile and drone attack against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure immediately after the partial ceasefire ends in late April while also stalling negotiations. ([ACAPS 13/09/2024](https://www.acaps.org/fileadmin/Data_Product/Main_media/20240913_ACAPS_Ukraine_Analysis_hub_Attacks_on_the_energy_infrastructure_in_Ukraine.pdf), [ACAPS 12/02/2025](https://www.acaps.org/fileadmin/Data_Product/Main_media/20250219_ACAPS_Ukraine_-_Energy_infrastructure_attacks-_Updated_outlook_and_impact_during_the_2024-2025_cold_season_.pdf), [Dixigroup 31/03/2025](https://dixigroup.org/en/analytic/russian-war-against-ukraine-energy-dimension-dixi-group-alert-weekly-review-93/), [Kyiv Independent 03/04/2025](https://kyivindependent.com/ukraine-informs-us-about-russias-energy-ceasefire-violations/))
